Belarusian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Ruthenian быкъ (byk), from Old East Slavic бꙑкъ (bykŭ), from Proto-Slavic *bykъ. Cognate with Ukrainian бик (byk).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [bɨk]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

бык • (byk) m animal (genitive быка́, nominative plural быкі́, genitive plural быко́ў)

  1. bull

Komi-Zyrian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbɯk/, [ˈbɯ̈k]
  • Rhymes: -ɯk
  • Hyphenation: бык

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian бык (byk).

Noun

[edit]

бык • (byk)

  1. (dialectal) synonym of ӧш (öš, “bull”)

Russian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • быкъ (byk) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic бꙑкъ (bykŭ), from Proto-Slavic *bykъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [bɨk]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɨk

Noun

[edit]

бык • (byk) m anim or m inan (genitive быка́, nominative plural быки́, genitive plural быко́в, relational adjective бы́чий or быча́чий, diminutive бычо́к, augmentative бычи́ще or быча́ра)

  1. (animate) bull, ox
  2. (animate, colloquial) a big, strong, or stubborn man
    Synonyms: здоровя́к (zdorovják), сила́ч (siláč)
  3. (animate, slang) gangster, mobster, soldier (rank-and-file member of a criminal gang)
    Synonym: банди́т (bandít)
  4. (animate, finance) bull
  5. (inanimate) abutment, pier
  6. (inanimate, regional) rocky headland

    • бы́чка f (býčka)

Yakut

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Turkic *bak- (“to look, to watch”).

Verb

[edit]

бык • (bïk)

  1. (intransitive) to appear
    Synonyms: баар буол (baar buol), көһүн (köhün)
    ый быкта ― ïy bïkta ― the moon appeared
  2. to peek / poke / stick out
